The CAP Theorem, Simply: storyboard

Episode 12 · voice Chris · 9 scenes · 80.8s (measured timing) · one still per beat, 8 frames after it fires

hook hook Stat · 0.0s–8.2s

Headline: Something has to give

“You can't have all three: consistency, availability and partition tolerance, so every big system picks two. Which would you pick?”

branding sting 8.2s–9.7s

Bite wipe → logos → cut. No voiceover, just the chomp.

idea idea Diorama · 9.7s–17.9s

Headline: Two branches, one line

“Eric Brewer framed it in two thousand. Picture two bank branches syncing your balance over one phone line.”

breakdown letters ThreeCards · 17.9s–29.4s

No headline

“Consistency means both branches show the same balance, availability means each one always answers, and partition tolerance means carrying on when that line goes dead.”

breakdown cut Sequence · 29.4s–38.4s

Headline: The line goes dead

“Networks do fail, so that last one isn't optional: you deposit fifty dollars at one branch, and the update never reaches the other.”

breakdown ask Sequence · 38.4s–44.6s

No headline

“Then you check your balance at the second branch, and it has to decide what to tell you without being able to ask.”

breakdown choice Split · 44.6s–55.0s

Headline: Wait, or guess?

“It can refuse until the line is back, correct but unavailable, like Google's Spanner, or answer with the old balance, available but briefly wrong, like Cassandra.”

breakdown nuance Decision · 55.0s–63.9s

Headline: Only when it breaks

“That's also why pick two is misleading: while the network is healthy you get both, and the choice only bites during a split.”

breakdown tune Cluster · 63.9s–73.9s

Headline: Dial it per call

“Modern databases let each request choose: read one copy for speed, or wait for a majority to agree, so carts and payments can pick differently.”

gist gist GistCard · 73.9s–80.8s

No headline

“That's the gist: when the network breaks, choose correct or available. Follow for more.”
